examples.ko: 아이가 엄마 손을 꼭 그러쥐고 놓지 않아요.
examples.en: The child grips her mom's hand tightly and won't let go.
It was cold, so I walked with both fists clenched.

examples.ko: 그는 화가 나서 주먹을 불끈 그러쥐었어요.
examples.en: He was angry and clenched his fist hard.

examples.ko: 동전을 손에 그러쥔 채 가게로 뛰어갔어요.
examples.en: I ran to the store with the coins clutched in my hand.
I was nervous and was gripping the hem of my clothes.

examples.ko: 아기가 제 손가락을 그러쥐니까 너무 귀여워요.
examples.en: It's so cute when the baby grips my finger.

explain: '잡다', '쥐다'보다 손에 힘을 주어 꽉 움켜잡는 느낌이 강해요. 주먹을 쥐거나 손에 든 것을 꼭 잡을 때 쓰고, 말보다는 글에서 더 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It feels stronger than '잡다' or '쥐다', as if you squeeze hard with your hand. It is used for clenching a fist or holding something tightly, and you will see it more in writing than in speech.

examples.ko: 그런저런 걱정을 할 사이도 없이 몹시 피곤했어요.
examples.en: I was so tired that I had no time to worry about this and that.
For one reason or another, I couldn't go to the gathering.

examples.ko: 그런저런 일들 때문에 요즘 정신이 없어요.
examples.en: I've been overwhelmed lately because of all sorts of things.
Don't pay attention to talk like that.

examples.ko: 그런저런 사정을 다 알고 나니 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: Once I knew all those circumstances, my heart ached.

examples.ko: 그런저런 준비를 하다 보니 벌써 저녁이 됐어요.
examples.en: While doing one preparation after another, it was already evening.

explain: '이런저런'처럼 여러 가지를 한꺼번에 말하는데, '그런저런'은 앞에서 이미 말한 것들을 가리킬 때 써요. 꾸며 주는 말이라 항상 뒤에 명사가 와요.
explain_en: Like '이런저런', it lumps several things together, but '그런저런' points back to things already mentioned. It modifies a noun, so a noun always follows it.

examples.en: Tears welled up in the child's eyes.

examples.ko: 그녀는 눈에 눈물이 그렁그렁한 채 웃었어요.
examples.en: She smiled with her eyes brimming with tears.

examples.ko: 동생이 눈에 눈물이 그렁그렁한 얼굴로 서 있었어요.
examples.en: My little brother stood there with a face and eyes brimming with tears.
Watching the sad movie, my eyes filled with tears.

examples.ko: 강아지가 눈에 눈물이 그렁그렁해서 저를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: The puppy looked at me with teary, brimming eyes.

examples.ko: 엄마 얼굴을 보자 눈에 눈물이 그렁그렁 고였어요.
examples.en: When I saw my mom's face, tears pooled in my eyes.

explain: 눈물이 눈에 가득 고였지만 아직 흐르지 않은 모습이에요. 이미 흘러내리는 모습은 '주르륵'이나 '펑펑'을 써요. 거의 '눈물'과만 짝이 돼요.
explain_en: It describes tears that have filled the eyes but have not fallen yet. For tears already running down, use '주르륵' or '펑펑'. It almost always pairs with '눈물' (tears).

examples.en: My pay is small, but I'm getting by somehow.
It was hard at first, but I got used to it somehow.
The whole day passed by somehow.

examples.ko: 시험은 그렁저렁 잘 본 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think I did okay on the exam.
How are you these days? I'm getting along so-so.

examples.ko: 그렁저렁 시간을 보내다 보니 방학이 끝났어요.
examples.en: Passing the time somehow, the vacation ended.

explain: 같은 뜻으로 '그럭저럭'도 써요. 아주 좋지도 나쁘지도 않게, 그냥 그렇게 지나가거나 지내는 모습을 말할 때 쓰고, 안부 대답으로 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '그럭저럭' is another form with the same meaning. It describes things going along neither very well nor badly, and it fits well as an answer to 'How are you?'.

examples.en: I sat and rested on a tree stump in the forest.

examples.ko: 나무를 베어 낸 자리에 그루터기만 남았어요.
examples.en: Only a stump was left where the tree had been cut.
A new sprout came up from the old stump.
A big stump sits there like a chair.
The kids climb up on the stump and play.

examples.ko: 그루터기의 나이테를 세어 보면 나무 나이를 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you count the rings on the stump, you can tell the tree's age.

explain: 나무나 풀을 베어 낸 뒤에 땅에 남은 부분을 말할 때 써요. 서 있는 나무의 아래쪽 줄기는 '밑동'이라고 해요.
explain_en: You use it for the part left in the ground after a tree or plant is cut down. The lower part of a tree that is still standing is called '밑동'.

examples.ko: 그물코가 너무 커서 작은 물고기는 빠져나가요.
examples.en: The mesh is so big that small fish slip through.

examples.ko: 어부가 찢어진 그물코를 한 땀씩 꿰맸어요.
examples.en: The fisherman mended the torn mesh stitch by stitch.
Sunlight shone through the holes of the net.
The tighter the mesh, the more fish you catch.
My finger got caught in the net and was hard to pull out.
This net has a really tight mesh.

explain: 그물에 뚫린 구멍 하나하나를 가리켜요. '촘촘하다', '성기다', '크다', '작다' 같은 말과 자주 같이 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to each hole in a net. It often appears with words like '촘촘하다' (tight), '성기다' (loose), '크다' (big) and '작다' (small).

en: last day of the lunar month

examples.ko: 음력 그믐에 할머니 댁에 가기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to visit Grandma's house on the last day of the lunar month.
Around the end of the lunar month, the moon is hardly visible.

examples.ko: 음력 그믐날 밤에는 하늘이 아주 어두워요.
examples.en: On the last night of the lunar month, the sky is very dark.

examples.ko: 그믐달이 새벽 하늘에 가늘게 떠 있어요.
examples.en: A thin waning crescent hangs in the dawn sky.
On a moonless night at month's end, the stars are easier to see.
It was the end of the month, so the road was pitch dark.

explain: 음력 한 달의 마지막 날이에요. 이날 밤에는 달이 거의 안 보여요. 달이 가장 둥근 '보름'과 짝으로 외우세요. 그믐 무렵에 뜨는 가는 달은 '그믐달'이에요.
explain_en: It is the last day of a lunar month, and the moon is barely visible that night. Learn it as a pair with '보름', when the moon is fullest. The thin moon seen around then is called '그믐달'.

en: around the end of the month

examples.en: I'm going to move around the end of this month.
I'll come visit you sometime around the end of the month.
My pay usually comes in around the end of the month.
It often snows around the end of December.
It's around the end of the month, so there's no moon in the night sky.

examples.ko: 그믐께에 맞춰 책을 다 읽으려고 해요.
examples.en: I'm trying to finish the book by around the end of the month.

explain: '그믐'에 '-께'가 붙어서 그믐 무렵을 말해요. 일상에서는 '월말쯤'이라고도 하고, 반대로 달의 중간쯤은 '보름께'라고 해요.
explain_en: '-께' is added to '그믐' to mean around the end of the month. In daily talk people also say '월말쯤', and the middle of the month is '보름께'.

examples.en: I singed my bangs while grilling meat.
I lightly toasted the seaweed over the fire and ate it.

examples.ko: 가스 불에 고추를 그슬어 껍질을 벗겼어요.
examples.en: I charred the pepper over the gas flame and peeled it.
My sleeve touched the candle and I ended up singeing it.

examples.ko: 토치로 겉면을 살짝 그슬면 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: It tastes better if you lightly sear the surface with a torch.

examples.ko: 고기 겉만 살짝 그슬어서 접시에 놓으세요.
examples.en: Lightly sear just the outside of the meat and put it on a plate.

explain: '태우다'와 달리 완전히 태우지 않고 겉만 살짝 타게 할 때 써요. 햇볕이나 연기에 검게 되는 것은 '그을리다'를 써요. 'ㄹ' 받침이라서 '그슨'처럼 ㄹ이 빠지는 활용에 주의하세요.
explain_en: Unlike '태우다' (to burn), it is for scorching only the surface lightly without burning it fully. For turning dark from sun or smoke, use '그을리다'. It has an ㄹ ending, so watch for ㄹ dropping in forms like '그슨'.

examples.en: A deep, gentle fragrance spread through the room.
He gazed at his wife with deep feeling.
It's a night when the moonlight shines softly.
The sound of a bell echoed deeply from the mountain temple.
The rich scent of coffee reached my nose.

examples.ko: 그분은 그윽이 웃으며 제 이야기를 들어 주셨어요.
examples.en: She listened to my story with a deep, gentle smile.

explain: 깊고 은은하게 느껴지는 모습이에요. 향기, 눈빛, 달빛, 소리 같은 말과 어울려요. '깊이'는 정도만 말하지만 '그윽이'는 고요하고 은은한 느낌이 더해져요.
explain_en: It describes something that feels deep and subtle. It goes with words like fragrance, gaze, moonlight and sound. '깊이' only speaks of degree, but '그윽이' adds a quiet, subtle feeling.

en: be tanned; be scorched; be blackened

examples.en: My face got very tanned from the sun.
Your sun-tanned skin looks healthy.
After playing on the beach, my face got tanned dark.
There was a fire, and the wall got blackened with soot.

examples.ko: 주방 천장이 연기에 그을려서 청소해야 해요.
examples.en: The kitchen ceiling is blackened by smoke, so I have to clean it.
Wear a hat so you don't get tanned.

explain: 햇볕이나 불, 연기 때문에 피부나 물건이 검게 변할 때 써요. 피부는 '피부가 타다'라고도 하고, 이미 변한 상태를 말할 때는 '그을린 얼굴'처럼 '그을린'을 써요.
explain_en: It is used when skin or objects turn dark because of sun, fire or smoke. For skin people also say '피부가 타다', and for the resulting state you say '그을린 얼굴' (a tanned face).

examples.ko: 촛불을 켜 두었더니 유리에 그을음이 생겼어요.
examples.en: I left a candle burning, and soot formed on the glass.

examples.ko: 오래된 난로에서 그을음이 나와 손에 묻었어요.
examples.en: Soot came out of the old stove and got on my hands.
A lot of soot has built up in the chimney.
Black soot has stuck to the bottom of the pot.
Smoke rose and soot formed on the ceiling.
I wiped the soot off my face with my hand.

explain: 불이 탈 때 생기는 검은 가루예요. '검댕'이라고도 하고, '그을리다'와 짝으로 외우면 쉬워요. 발음은 [그으름]이에요.
explain_en: It is the black powder produced when something burns. It is also called '검댕', and it is easy to learn together with '그을리다'. It is pronounced [그으름].

examples.ko: 아이의 웃음을 보니 마음이 그지없이 행복했어요.
examples.en: Seeing the child's smile, I felt endlessly happy.
I'm immensely grateful for that person's kindness.
I was overjoyed at the news that I passed.
Parents' love is boundlessly deep.
It was an endlessly clear autumn sky.
Coming back home after so long, I feel utterly at ease.

explain: '한없이'와 비슷하게 끝이 없을 만큼 정도가 크다는 느낌이에요. 기쁘다, 고맙다, 행복하다 같은 좋은 감정과 많이 쓰고, '반갑기 그지없어요'처럼 '-기 그지없다' 꼴로도 써요.
explain_en: Like '한없이', it gives a feeling of having no limit. It is often used with good feelings such as glad, grateful and happy, and also appears in the pattern '-기 그지없다', as in '반갑기 그지없어요'.

examples.en: When I offered a gift, they firmly declined.

examples.ko: 친구는 자기 잘못이 아니라고 극구 말했어요.
examples.en: My friend insisted vehemently that it wasn't their fault.

examples.ko: 할머니는 용돈을 안 받겠다고 극구 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma insisted strongly that she wouldn't take the pocket money.
Everyone tried hard to stop him, but he left.
The teacher praised that book highly.

examples.ko: 제가 계산한다고 했더니 그분이 극구 말리셨어요.
examples.en: When I said I'd pay, they strongly objected.

explain: 사양하다, 말리다, 칭찬하다, 부인하다 같은 말 앞에서 '있는 힘을 다해서'라는 느낌을 더해요. 주로 말하는 행동에 쓰고, 보통 '극구 사양하다'처럼 한 덩어리로 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Before verbs such as decline, stop, praise and deny, it adds the feeling of 'with all one's might'. It is mainly used for speech-related actions, and often appears as a set phrase like '극구 사양하다'.

examples.en: This app maximizes user convenience.
They raised the price to maximize profit.

examples.ko: 공부 효과를 극대화하려면 충분히 자야 해요.
examples.en: To maximize your study results, you need enough sleep.

examples.ko: 감독은 선수들의 장점을 극대화하는 작전을 짰어요.
examples.en: The coach made a plan that maximizes the players' strengths.

examples.ko: 햇빛을 많이 받도록 창을 크게 내서 채광을 극대화했어요.
examples.en: They made big windows to maximize natural light.

examples.ko: 재미를 극대화하기 위해 마지막에 반전을 넣었어요.
examples.en: They added a twist at the end to maximize the fun.

explain: '최대로 하다'를 한 단어로 말하는 거예요. 효과, 이익, 재미, 효율 같은 말과 자주 쓰여요. 반대말은 '극소화하다'나 '최소화하다'이고, 뉴스나 설명하는 글에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is a one-word way to say 'make as large as possible'. It often goes with effect, profit, fun and efficiency. The opposites are '극소화하다' and '최소화하다', and it appears a lot in news and explanatory writing.

examples.en: Citizens fiercely opposed the plan.

examples.ko: 두 팀의 응원전이 극렬해서 경기장이 시끄러웠어요.
examples.en: The cheering battle between the two teams was so intense that the stadium was loud.
The plan was delayed after running into fierce backlash.
The conflict between the two grew more and more intense.
The residents protested the construction furiously.
The argument became so fierce that the meeting was stopped.

explain: 반대, 저항, 반발, 갈등이 몹시 거세다고 말할 때 써요. '격렬하다'와 뜻이 가깝지만 '극렬하다'는 반대나 항의처럼 부딪치는 일에 주로 쓰고, 기쁜 일에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is used when opposition, resistance, backlash or conflict is extremely fierce. It is close to '격렬하다', but '극렬하다' is mainly used for clashes such as objections and protests, and not for happy things.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 성격 차이가 극명히 드러났어요.
examples.en: The difference in the two people's personalities became strikingly clear.

examples.ko: 이 사진이 그날의 상황을 극명히 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This photo shows the situation that day very clearly.
The results were so starkly different that everyone was surprised.

examples.ko: 이 실험은 그 차이를 극명히 증명했어요.
examples.en: This experiment proved that difference unmistakably.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 생활 모습이 극명히 대비돼요.
examples.en: The way of life in the two countries contrasts sharply.

examples.ko: 점수가 극명히 갈린 걸 보면 준비 차이가 컸어요.
examples.en: Seeing how sharply the scores split, the difference in preparation was big.

explain: 차이나 모습이 아주 뚜렷하게 보일 때 써요. 주로 '드러나다', '보여 주다', '대비되다', '갈리다' 같은 말과 함께 나와요. 말할 때는 '극명하게'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when a difference or appearance is very clear. It mostly appears with words like '드러나다' (be revealed), '보여 주다' (show), '대비되다' (contrast) and '갈리다' (split). In speech people also say '극명하게'.

examples.en: The government increased support for the poorest people.

examples.ko: 극빈층 아이들에게 무료 급식을 해 줘요.
examples.en: They provide free meals to children from the poorest families.
Every winter, donations to help the poorest keep coming in.

examples.ko: 이 단체는 극빈층 가정에 쌀을 나눠 줘요.
examples.en: This group hands out rice to households in extreme poverty.
I hear the number of people in the poorest class is growing.

examples.ko: 극빈층의 생활 안정을 위한 정책이 필요해요.
examples.en: Policies are needed to stabilize the lives of the poorest.

explain: 뉴스나 정책 이야기에서 나오는 말이에요. '빈곤층'과 비슷하지만 그보다 더 어려운 사람들을 가리켜요. '중산층', '상류층'과 함께 사회 계층을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It appears in news and policy discussion. It is close to '빈곤층' but points to people in even harder circumstances. It is used with '중산층' (middle class) and '상류층' (upper class) when talking about social classes.

examples.en: That family's kid is really hyper and pushy.
The child is having a hard time because of overbearing parents.
Our puppy runs around in such a wild way.

examples.ko: 동생이 극성맞게 졸라서 결국 사 줬어요.
examples.en: My little brother pestered me so relentlessly that I ended up buying it.

examples.ko: 극성맞은 팬들이 가수 집 앞에서 기다렸어요.
examples.en: Obsessive fans waited in front of the singer's house.

examples.ko: 극성맞게 굴지 말고 얌전히 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: Don't be so wild; sit still and behave.

explain: 성격이 드세고 지나치게 열심이거나 부산스러운 사람이나 동물에게 써요. 칭찬보다는 조금 못마땅한 느낌이 있어요. 비슷하게 '극성스럽다'도 써요.
explain_en: It describes people or animals that are pushy, overly zealous or restless. It carries a slightly disapproving feeling rather than praise. '극성스럽다' is used in a similar way.
